discovery: Detection of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale galaxy distribution, establishing a standard ruler for cosmic expansion

nominees.name: Daniel J. Eisenstein
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

motivation: In 2005 two independent surveys, SDSS (Eisenstein et al.) and the 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey (Cole, Peacock et al.), detected the imprint of primordial sound waves in the clustering of galaxies. Eisenstein also developed much of the theory and method that made the feature usable. The acoustic scale, set in the early-universe plasma and calibrated by the CMB, gives a geometric standard ruler that is unusually robust to astrophysical systematics. It confirmed the gravitational-instability picture linking the CMB to today's structure, independently supported cosmic acceleration, and became the backbone of BOSS, eBOSS, Euclid and DESI. The 2024-25 DESI results, which hint at evolving dark energy, show that BAO is now a precision test of the standard model itself. Eisenstein led the theory and the SDSS detection; Cole and Peacock led the 2dFGRS power-spectrum analysis that independently confirmed it.
